reviews.text: We travelled from White Plains to Midwood for an international travel health certificate. The staff was friendly, professional, and knew all the regulatory requirements. The clinic was comfortable, clean, and modern. If we lived closer we would go to Ivy Pets for routine care, but we will definitely return for travel veterinary care.

I came in with concerns of my Maltese itching after a flea treatment ,worried about his skin and possible being re-infected due to the area that I live in. Vanessa was such a major help. She ease my worries and my anxiety, I was able to get good tips and a little education over other options that I have for treatments. She really eased my worries ans someone with really bad anxiety and the care that she gave my Metro was a 10 out of 10.  she went a little bit more than above and beyond compared other groomers and technicians I’ve dealt with. Even offering to shave him to make it easier for me, since I’m low vision and I really appreciate her work. I care more about my dog being healthy than him looking pretty and I’m glad that she understood where I was coming from with some of my concerns. I didn’t feel like I was talking to a wall at all like I had with other vets in the 10 years that I’ve had him. I’m so glad to make this my permanent vet clinic for my baby. Outside of just her amazing work and other doctors that I’ve dealt with on my first visit who were also amazing. The front desk is also super nice and I did have a chance to speak with the groomer my first visit and I really loved her energy too, so I cannot wait to continue coming here. It’s only been my second visit. I’ll definitely be back.
Affordable and very friendly!
Horrible! Priority is money not your pets health.

I reached out after hours last night and had a rocky first encounter with the person I spoke with by phone. I simply hung up and called another practice. While I was on that call, however, I received a voicemail from Catherine, the practice manager. She had apparently overheard the call I was part of, recognized that there were areas for improvement, and took it upon herself to reach out. Based entirely on her professionalism and sincerity, I decided to take a chance and still come in—and I am SO glad I did.

I genuinely felt like we received VIP service. Beyond this being an upscale practice with exam rooms nicer than any room I have personally been examined in, what stood out most was the service recovery. Catherine identified that something had gone wrong, proactively called to apologize and correct any misinformation or misunderstanding, and made Hope an appointment for that evening. Now mind you, I had not even complained. They could have simply gone about their business, but instead they worked hard to make it right. When it comes to Vanessa, I think Catherine, she's really just like that about her job.

Catherine met with me personally when we arrived. Every question and concern I had about my girl was answered with patience and kindness. Catherines humility really shines through and her genuine care and respect show very easily if you speak to her for even a minute. The veterinarian was a very sweet man with a ton of experience, and everyone, from Cathering to the best tech Vanessa, but also the super cool and funny, friendly women who checked me out, one of whom may even have been the person I initially got off on the wrong foot with, made me feel comfortable and respected. The entire practice is exceptionally professionally run, but the care still felt genuinely warm and customized to Hope.

Vanessa, the technician assigned to us, called me twice while reviewing Hope’s records and personally contacted FOUR If not five different veterinary practices—in Long Beach, Scarsdale, Marine Park and Denver—to track down the information needed for Hope’s international travel. I later learned that she had skipped her lunch to make those calls. Oh, then she accommodated me with an earlier appointment time because it was available and more convenient for me.  Talk about above and beyond all day. Whether Vanessa was asked to be extra nice or not, she did far more than her job required her to do and it really helped me out. A lot.

We addressed several vaccines that day, but when I said I preferred not to do a specific vaccination, I received absolutely zero pushback. I never felt as though they were trying to sell me treatments or procedures that were not clinically indicated. On the contrary, I felt they were actively trying to help me avoid unnecessary expenses. They educated me, allowed me to make informed choices, and still ensured that my dog’s needs were fully attended to.

I initially needed this practice because they have USDA-accredited veterinarians who can facilitate international travel documents and the prerequisite care. If I were not relocating, this would absolutely become the primary practice for my almost-11-year-old pup. I will still be retaining them as our US veterinary practice because I was that pleased with the care, professionalism and service recovery.

I have been to concierge and boutique veterinary practices before. Ivy Pet is very reasonably priced for the caliber of care it delivers and the atmosphere it provides for the animals we love.

If you are considering this practice for international travel certification or any of the procedures required for travel, I strongly recommend the Avenue M location. International travel with a pet is hard enough; it is a huge relief to know that I can travel confidently after working with this team.Any information they didn’t know or have they made a point of finding out before I arrived.

Class act, concierge-level care and service—and my dog happily let them stick her with needles. What more can you ask for?

I strongly advise against using this office for anything more complex than basic services. My cat has inflamed gums, so I specifically notified them about it and called to schedule a dental cleaning, dental checkup, and X-rays. Once in the office, the doctor provided a basic physical checkup and was unable to identify the cause of the inflammation. He suggested waiting for another doctor to return on a later date, potential tooth removal, or simply waiting until the cat starts showing signs of pain. They do not have an X-ray machine on site and cannot perform a dental cleaning. Essentially, the visit was a waste of time. I left with no new information beyond what I already knew. If you cannot provide the requested service, you should not mislead clients and sell an unnecessary basic physical exam.

I brought in a feral FIV+ cat with gingivitis/stomatitis, and before recommending or performing any diagnostics, Dr. SanGeorgio visually declared it “cancer” and advised either removing his jaw or euthanasia. I was stunned that these were the only two options presented. A friend urged me to request a biopsy — and I’m so grateful I did, because it proved the diagnosis was incorrect. It was not cancer, and those extreme recommendations were completely unnecessary.

Aside from neutering him — which they performed while wearing full hazmat suits, an excessive and alarming measure — this clinic provided no meaningful help. They refused to remove the mass in his mouth, refused to prescribe a low dose steroid, and would not even administer a steroid injection. It took me three weeks of back and forth just to obtain basic medications such as anti-inflammatories, gabapentin, and amoxicillin, and even those were eventually cut off.

I will never return, and I do not recommend this clinic to anyone. If you do go, ALWAYS get a second opinion. Their approach and judgment were consistently lacking.

To Lenni and Dr. SanGeorgio: Tabby is thriving now. We took him to another veterinary practice — one that genuinely cares — and he finally received the proper treatment he deserved.

Ivy Pets is only suitable for the most basic, surface level care. Do not go here if your animal requires expert or in depth treatment. They operate like a corporation focused on rapid profit, not true veterinary medicine, and their care reflects that.
